fact: The RNPP holds citizens' biometric and civil data and assigns each person a national identification number (NNI), according to the article.
Linfodrome reports ONECI's director general presenting Cote d'Ivoire's identification system, run by the single office ONECI, as a strategic state infrastructure.
ONECI manages the RNPP and assigns the national identification number, per the PARAE coordinator.
ONECI enrols applicants and issues the national identity card, with a stamp bought online, enrolment at an approved centre and a notification to collect the produced card.
Biometric Update describes the RNPP as ONECI's biometric register of natural persons, to which MaPoste is linked.
ONECI's director general says the RNPP gives each citizen an NNI based on biometric data.
ONECI says citizens can obtain a personal, secure and permanent National Identification Number (NNI), and applicants for the national ID card are invited to enrol for it.
ONECI's director general said on 16 September 2025 that national identification numbers (NNI) have been attributed to more than 9 million people.

ONECI's slides for ID4Africa 2026 report 172 fixed identity enrolment centres plus mobile enrolment units and intensified enrolment campaigns, and call the unique identifier an essential structuring element.

ONECI deputy director general Pélagie Gonto said in October 2024 that national identity cards are issued under the national register of persons project, with a national number (NNI) that stays unchanged for each person for life, and that 8 million people are in ONECI's base.
ONECI manages Cote d'Ivoire's national ID and biometric identification systems, per Biometric Update.
